note.explanation: Organising data makes it clearer, quicker to use and easier to analyse. Data can be collected using methods such as surveys, questionnaires, interviews and observations, then organised into tables, charts or graphs. Information from online sources can be extracted and integrated to build a fuller understanding of a topic.
examples: A table of students' marks makes it easier to compare their scores in different subjects.
For a project on social media, you could collect information from several websites, save relevant statistics and combine similar findings.
note.checkAnswer: Organising data into tables, charts and graphs makes it clearer and easier to find, compare and analyse.
note.simple: Put information in a neat, useful form so it is easier to understand and compare.
note.checkQuestion: Why can organising data into tables or charts help when analysing it?
note.title: Organising and Analysing Data
steps: Collect information using a suitable method, such as a survey or observation.
Arrange the information neatly in a table, chart or graph.
Look for patterns, trends or similarities.
Combine useful information from different sources when a fuller picture is needed.

written.text: Explain the concept of data visualization. How does it help in understanding complex data? Provide examples of different types of visualizations and their applications in real-life scenarios.
written.finalAnswer: Data visualization presents data visually, using forms such as charts and graphs, to make information easier to understand. It can help people identify patterns and trends in complex data. For example, a bar chart can compare categories such as students' subject scores, a line graph can show changes over time, and a pie chart can show parts of a whole such as the shares of different phone brands.

explain.title: Why organise data?
explain.body: Organising data neatly can reduce errors, save time and make information clearer. Tables, charts and graphs help readers compare information and see what the data is saying.

explain.title: Collecting data
explain.body: Data collection is the process of gathering information to answer questions, make decisions, or understand something better. Methods include surveys, questionnaires, interviews, observations and online data sources.

explain.title: Finding and combining information
explain.body: Data extraction means finding and saving the most relevant information from a larger set of data. Data integration combines information from different sources to get a complete perspective.

explain.title: Presenting and interpreting results
explain.body: Arrange the data in a useful form, such as a table, chart or graph. Then compare the information, look for common themes or trends, and summarise what it shows.

mistakes: Writing that organisation only makes data look neat, without explaining that it also helps reduce errors, save time or analyse information.
Confusing data extraction with data integration: extraction selects relevant information; integration combines information from sources.
Giving a survey example without explaining how the responses will be collected and analysed.
Naming a chart or graph without stating what information it displays or what it helps the reader understand.
Copying information from online sources without keeping it organised by topic or source.
